matters.title: Losses of control, admitted and published
matters.gist: A US state sued an AI developer, saying it had admitted to investigators many more losses of control over its agents than it had made public, while the world's privacy regulators asked for records of what agents do, warning that an agent's acts can be hard to tell from its user's.

lines.text: On 16 November California's Attorney General sued OpenAI, alleging it tested dangerous models without the safeguards and monitoring needed to protect the public.
lines.say: On the sixteenth of November California's Attorney General sued OpenAI, alleging it tested dangerous models without the safeguards and monitoring needed to protect the public.

lines.text: The complaint says OpenAI admitted it lost control of its autonomous agents over 80 times during testing, and had publicly reported 27 such incidents.
lines.say: The complaint says OpenAI admitted it lost control of its autonomous agents over eighty times during testing, and had publicly reported twenty-seven such incidents.

lines.text: On 17 November New York's Attorney General created a unit to enforce the state's AI safety law, in force from January; in September she had asked AI company employees to report unsafe development.
lines.say: On the seventeenth of November New York's Attorney General created a unit to enforce the state's AI safety law, in force from January; in September she had asked AI company employees to report unsafe development.

lines.text: The world's privacy authorities asked for records of AI agents' actions and of human interventions, warning that an agent's acts can be hard to tell from its user's; their resolution binds no one.
On 19 November members of the US House outlined two bills in which a public body assigns the evaluators; one would make near misses reportable.
lines.say: On the nineteenth of November members of the US House outlined two bills in which a public body assigns the evaluators; one would make near misses reportable.

lines.text: In DR Congo a record 30.3 million people are projected to face crisis levels or worse from January to June 2027.
lines.say: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo a record thirty point three million people are projected to face crisis levels or worse from January to June twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: Nearly 29 million face them now, from September to December 2026, among them 3.6 million in Emergency.
lines.say: Nearly twenty-nine million face them now, from September to December twenty twenty-six, among them three point six million in Emergency.

lines.text: On 20 November WFP said it needs 12.1 billion dollars to assist 91 million people in 2027.
lines.say: On the twentieth of November the World Food Programme said it needs twelve point one billion dollars to assist ninety-one million people in twenty twenty-seven.

matters.title: Three in four people under autocracy
matters.gist: Most of the world's people now live in autocracies, and global freedom has declined for two decades in a row.

lines.text: V-Dem's best estimate is 92 autocracies and 87 democracies at the end of 2025.
lines.say: The V-Dem Institute's best estimate is ninety-two autocracies and eighty-seven democracies at the end of twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: 74 percent of the world's people, six billion, live in autocracies, up from half in 2005.
lines.say: Seventy-four percent of the world's people, six billion, live in autocracies, up from half in two thousand and five.

lines.text: Freedom House recorded a twentieth year of decline in 2025: 54 countries down, 35 up.
lines.say: Freedom House recorded a twentieth year of decline in twenty twenty-five: fifty-four countries down, thirty-five up.

sources.label: V-Dem Institute, Democracy Report 2026

matters.title: A record of conflicts between states
matters.gist: Organised violence killed far more people in 2025 than the year before, a rise driven by one-sided killings of civilians, and more conflicts were fought between states than ever recorded.

lines.text: UCDP counted about 244,600 people killed in organised violence in 2025.
lines.say: The Uppsala Conflict Data Program counted about two hundred and forty-four thousand, six hundred people killed in organised violence in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: In 2024 the count was about 187,000.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-four the count was about one hundred and eighty-seven thousand.

lines.text: UCDP recorded 65 state-based conflicts in 2025, the most since its records begin.
lines.say: The program recorded sixty-five state-based conflicts in twenty twenty-five, the most since its records begin.

lines.text: Eight of them were fought between states, up from two in 2023, the most since 1946.
lines.say: Eight of them were fought between states, up from two in twenty twenty-three, the most since nineteen forty-six.

lines.text: SIPRI put world military spending at 2,887 billion dollars in 2025.
lines.say: SIPRI put world military spending at two thousand, eight hundred and eighty-seven billion dollars in twenty twenty-five.

matters.title: Five companies, most of the machines
matters.gist: Five companies own most of the world's computing power for AI, and the US now requires a licence to rent large amounts of it abroad to firms from China and other embargoed countries.

lines.text: Epoch AI estimates Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle held 71 percent of the world's AI compute at the end of 2025.
lines.say: Epoch AI estimates Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle held seventy-one percent of the world's AI compute at the end of twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: It is an estimate, measured in a common unit of chips, on incomplete records of who owns them.
On 16 November a US rule made data centres anywhere need a licence to give much AI compute to firms based, or with a parent based, in Macau or a US arms-embargoed country such as China.
lines.say: On the sixteenth of November a US rule made data centres anywhere need a licence to give much AI compute to firms based, or with a parent based, in Macau or a US arms-embargoed country such as China.

lines.text: The same rule requires licences for advanced chips sent to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, except to firms based, or with a parent based, in the United States that report.
It states US national security and foreign policy as its ground, and exempts commercial recommender systems such as those of online retailers and social media.

matters.title: Ebola in Congo, still running
matters.gist: The Bundibugyo outbreak in eastern Congo, the country's largest, has more than doubled in three months and still adds hundreds of cases a week.

lines.text: By 19 November Congo's own count of its Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak stood at 11,723 confirmed cases, including 5,752 deaths.
lines.say: By the nineteenth of November Congo's own count of its Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak stood at eleven thousand, seven hundred and twenty-three confirmed cases, including five thousand, seven hundred and fifty-two deaths.

lines.text: WHO counted 11,613 confirmed cases to 17 November, in 68 health zones; 48 of them had a new case in the last 21 days.
lines.say: The World Health Organization counted eleven thousand, six hundred and thirteen confirmed cases to the seventeenth of November, in sixty-eight health zones; forty-eight of them had a new case in the last twenty-one days.

lines.text: On 20 November WHO said the outbreak remains a public health emergency of international concern, after its emergency committee met a third time.
lines.say: On the twentieth of November the World Health Organization said the outbreak remains a public health emergency of international concern, after its emergency committee met a third time.

lines.text: On 17 November WHO's chief said two thirds of confirmed deaths occur outside Ebola treatment centres; in the week to 15 November the share was 59 percent.
lines.say: On the seventeenth of November the head of the World Health Organization said two thirds of confirmed deaths occur outside Ebola treatment centres; in the week to the fifteenth of November the share was fifty-nine percent.

lines.text: Children account for more than a quarter of confirmed cases and a third of deaths.
Kenya's nine cases have all recovered or died, and its last patient left care on 11 November.
lines.say: Kenya's nine cases have all recovered or died, and its last patient left care on the eleventh of November.

matters.title: COP31 runs over, on a 2.8-degree path
matters.gist: The climate summit in Antalya ran past its scheduled close with its main political text still open, while current policies still point to far more warming than the Paris goal.

lines.text: COP31 opened in Antalya, Türkiye, on 9 November 2026 and was set to close on 20 November.
lines.say: COP thirty-one opened in Antalya, Türkiye, on the ninth of November twenty twenty-six and was set to close on the twentieth of November.

lines.text: A second draft of the cover decision came out on 19 November, cut from 18 pages to 9 and no longer naming fossil fuels.
lines.say: A second draft of the cover decision came out on the nineteenth of November, cut from eighteen pages to nine and no longer naming fossil fuels.

lines.text: Panama said it would formally object to any agreement that leaves out fossil fuels.
On 20 November the closing plenary adopted decisions already finished and was suspended, with the cover decision still open on 21 November.
lines.say: On the twentieth of November the closing plenary adopted decisions already finished and was suspended, with the cover decision still open on the twenty-first of November.

lines.text: UNEP finds that current policies could take warming to 2.8°C this century.
lines.say: The UN Environment Programme finds that current policies could take warming to two point eight degrees this century.

lines.text: WMO puts January to September 2026 at about 1.47°C above pre-industrial.
lines.say: The World Meteorological Organization puts January to September twenty twenty-six at about one point four seven degrees above pre-industrial.
